name: New York
originNote: LaGuardia, midpoint of runway 13/31, from FAA runway geometry.
The origin is an airfield rather than the middle of the map because world (0,0)
is where the aircraft starts and where floating-point precision is best, and
because an origin tied to a published surveyed thing can be checked.
extentNote: 30 nm half-width: the same 60 nm map the authored world uses, so §7's spacing rules and the LOD rings carry over unchanged.

tiers.note: 60 m matches the innermost LOD ring in mesh.ts exactly; finer cannot be drawn. Centred between Manhattan and the three airports, which is the ground actually flown.
Everything else, including the whole coarse LOD ring, which reaches past the map edge.

surface.note: Twice the finest elevation cell. Land cover is flat colour, so it survives being coarser than the heightfield; a crisper coastline is worth more than a crisper park boundary.

buildings.note: Six storeys and up. The core holds over a million footprints; at 20 m it holds about twenty thousand, which is a skyline rather than a city plan.

cityFromBuildings.note: Dense ground is derived from where the tall buildings actually are, rather than from landuse tags. Manhattan is largely tagged residential in OSM and would otherwise render as suburb.

airfieldTier.note: Every airfield the tiers above do not reach gets its own 60 m tier, 8 km across. A runway resolved only by the 240 m tier cannot be flattened properly — the flat pad is barely one cell wide — and Westchester sits at 134 m in hill country. About 20 KB each.
